dplyr's "Join columns must be unique" check (check_join_vars())

Source: R/join.R
check_join_cols_unique.Rd

Per side, equi columns plus the UNIQUE non-equi columns must not repeat: a column may appear in several non-equi conditions (join_by(a >= lo, a <= hi)) but not twice among the equi ones, nor in both an equi and a non-equi condition. dplyr raises a plain rlang_error; x is checked before y. Runs on the raw by at the verb call (before routing to the fallback), so eager, lazy and fallback joins all fail the same way. Also raises dplyr's keep = FALSE + non-equi error first, and, per side after its duplicates, dplyr's "Join columns in x must be present in the data." (so x's missing column precedes y's duplicates, as in dplyr's join_cols()).

Usage

check_join_cols_unique(
  by,
  x,
  keep = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  y = NULL
)

Arguments

by

The user's by= (NULL, character, join_by())

x

The left table

keep

The user's keep= (NULL for filtering joins)

call

The verb's frame, reported as the error call

y

The right table, or NULL to leave its columns unchecked
